questions.hint: Divide the suspect gap by the overall range.

questions.explanation: For Dixon's Q test the experimental statistic is the gap between the suspect value and its nearest neighbor divided by the full range of the data. A truncated range or an inverted ratio does not compare correctly with tabulated critical Q values.
